newsitem.title: UK: BA to sell its $400 mln stake in USAir.
newsitem.headline: BA to sell its $400 mln stake in USAir.

text.p: British Airways Plc put its 24.6 percent stake in USAir Group up for sale on Wednesday, signalling the beginning of the end of its unhappy three-year relationship with the U.S. domestic carrier.
BA said in a statement that if USAir did not take up its option to buy back the stake within 60 days then BA would make a public offering.
The move had been expected since the two airlines fell out this year over BA's plans to tie up with the much bigger carrier American Airlines.

"British Airways has taken this action with regret. But it has become inevitable. It would clearly be unwise to pursue an alliance with an unwilling partner," BA's chief executive Bob Ayling said in a statement.

BA's share price edged up 9 to 600-1/2p after the news as it raised hopes that by cutting USAir loose, BA and American had improved their chances of getting the U.S. authorites to pass their own controversial deal under anti-trust laws.

But analysts warned that having broken off with USAir there is a risk that BA could end up alone in the all-important transatlantic market if the US and European competition authorities decide to block the alliance with American.

"Most people are reading the move as BA signalling that they expect the American deal to get the go-ahead...but the risk is still there that they will be left without a partner next year," said Mike Powell, European airlines analyst at NatWest Markets.
The risk was there ever since USAir announced in October that it would end its code-sharing pact and frequent flier programme connection with BA at the end of March 1997.
Incensed by BA's romance with American, USAir is suing BA in a U.S. federal court on allegations of breach of agreement.
BA bought the shareholding for $400 million in 1993.
"The sale is simply acknowledgement that the relationship with USAir was over and was no point in tying up the capital any further," said, Nick Cunningham, analyst at BZW.
Ayling said the decision to shed the USAir stake was not related to the lawsuit, which he said British Airways still believed was groundless.

USAir has applied to operate its own transatlantic routes but it will not be able to secure access to London Heathrow without Britain and the U.S. agreeing a new open skies aviation services pact and agreement is in turn linked to BA and American getting their deal approved.
